name: Morgan Hamada
life: “I still remember the smell of sawdust in my first expensive office.” Monday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Morgan stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I built boats before I sold expensive moorings. I found myself checking this man's cupboards to see if he really lived here.
appearance: Morgan has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose. Look for a long silver braid. Back on the street, the familiar outfit is a narrow-striped sweater with a little coil of soft measuring tape. In conversation Morgan draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting.
personality: Morgan thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Morgan sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To recognize the resident's home without inspecting private cupboards.
family: Billie Warren is Morgan’s younger cousin. Morgan chooses the music. Billie puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The spare spectacles*, Billie says, “I translated the printed words. She corrected the name of the crossing in both languages.”
connections: Drew Hayward. A marina developer and an equipment coordinator have to turn a store back into a room.
